title: Car Seat Safety
hook: The car seat protects best when three things line up: rear-facing for as long as the seat allows, a harness snug enough you can't pinch the strap, and the back seat.
key_points: Keep your child rear-facing as long as possible — until they hit the top height or weight your seat's manufacturer allows.
A snug harness means you can't pinch any slack at the shoulder; the chest clip sits level with the armpits.
No bulky coats under the harness — they compress in a crash and leave the straps too loose; layer thin, then add a blanket over the buckled straps.
Register the seat and check for recalls, and ride all kids under 13 in the back seat.
content_html: A car seat does its job best when a few basics line up. Keep your child rear-facing as long as you can — the American Academy of Pediatrics says to stay rear-facing until your child reaches the highest weight or height the seat's manufacturer allows, not just a birthday. Then dial in the fit: the harness should be snug enough that you can't pinch a fold of strap at the shoulder, with the chest clip centered at armpit level.
extra_html: Two more things matter a lot. Skip bulky coats under the harness — the AAP warns they compress in a crash and leave the straps too loose, so dress your baby in thin layers and add a coat or blanket over the buckled straps instead. Finally, register the seat (online or by mailing the card) so you'll hear about recalls, check for recalls periodically, and keep every child under 13 in the back seat. This is general guidance — consider a certified car seat check and a hands-on infant first-aid/CPR class, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

flashcards.prompt: How do you know a car seat harness is snug enough?

choices.text: You can't pinch any slack in the strap at the shoulder
It looks roughly tight from across the room
There's room for a thick winter coat underneath

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP's pinch test: if you can pinch a fold of webbing at the shoulder, the harness is too loose.

flashcards.prompt: Why shouldn't a child wear a bulky coat under the car seat harness?
flashcards.back_html: The coat compresses in a crash, leaving the straps too loose to hold the child. Dress them in thin layers and tuck a coat or blanket over the buckled harness instead.

flashcards.prompt: How long should a young child stay rear-facing?

choices.text: As long as possible — up to the seat's top height or weight limit
Only until their first birthday, then turn them around
Until they can sit up unassisted

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP recommends keeping children rear-facing until they reach the highest weight or height their seat's manufacturer allows.
